content_html_sanitized:
Posted August 4, 2003
Last week, I reported that with George (Top Gun) Bush looking vulnerable, most of the candidates for the 2004 Democratic Presidential nomination seemed to be indicating support for medical marijuana. And a bill to keep the DEA from attacking medical cannabis patients did better than expected in the House.
See
Learning About Prohibitionism: House Debate on Medical Marijuana Bill Offers New Insight Into Police State Ideology.

Now, Americans for Safe Access reports that the California Democratic Council (a coalition of 125 democratic clubs) adopted ASA's resolution endorsing medical marijuana yesterday.

ASA's Steph Sherer says that this means medical marijuana will be on their agenda for the 2004 elections, and they will make recommendations to the state and national Democratic platform committees about including MMJ!

The resolution reads:

Resolved, that we call upon our elected officials to do all of the
following:
a) Respect the First Amendment rights of physicians who recommend medical
cannabis for their patients;
b) Immediately pass federal legislation that would allow individual states
to approve and enact medical cannabis laws;
c) Cease all prosecutions of legally qualified medical cannabis patients in
states which have medical cannabis laws; and
d) Reform federal laws to allow for the legal cultivation of medical
cannabis and its provision in a safe and orderly manner.

Getting the California vote is vital to any presidential candidate, so this is a real worry for the prohibitionists. It is still amazes me that it is considered daring to support something favored by an overwhelming majority of the people.

It will be interesting to see how long Senator Diane Feinstein will continue to betray her constituents. It is hard to believe that she is a former mayor of San Francisco.
See
The Hatch-Feinstein Methamphetamine Anti-Proliferation Act of 1999
Will Censor The Internet, Make It A Federal Crime To Teach Farmers To Grow Hemp, Or To Tell Medical Marijuana Patients How To Use or Grow Marijuana,
Or Even To Link To A Site Selling Pipes!

She and Senator Barbara Boxer failed to oppose Karen Tandy, the new head of the DEA, even though Tandy is necessarily a party-line opponent of medical cannabis, who said that there will be no let up in the Bush war against the sick and dying.

Meanwhile, an unscientific online poll of doctors taken by Medscape, showed that 76% of doctors and 89% of nurses favor medical access to cannabis. This is not a fluke. Two years ago, a similar poll showed similar results, although this time there were almost three times as many respondents, (6,461) so these results are likely to be representative of the medical profession.

If the Democrats can discover democracy, maybe the Republicans will discover the public interest.

The narcocracy is slowly losing its grip on DEAland. We are winning!
